name: 2N404
description: One of the most widely used general-purpose germanium PNP transistors of the early 1960s, still in production today by Central Semiconductor as a direct legacy part. Historically significant as the transistor in the Maestro Fuzz-Tone FZ-1 (1962), the first mass-produced guitar fuzz pedal. Low absolute ratings (25V, 100mA, 150mW) by modern standards; this is a small-signal/low-power switching part, not a power device.

pins.name: E
pins.description: emitter; lead nearest the case tab

TO-5.notes: Standard TO-5 metal can, bottom view. Small tab on the case rim near lead 1 (emitter) at roughly 45 degrees from the lead 1-3 centerline, the usual TO-5/TO-18 orientation key. Leads 1-2-3 (E-B-C) arranged in a triangle per Central Semiconductor's own mechanical outline drawing.

extra.hFE: 30 min @ Vce=0.15V, Ic=12mA (24 min @ Vce=0.2V, Ic=24mA; 135 typ small-signal @ Vcb=6V, Ic=1mA, f=1kHz)
extra.Vce(sat): 0.15V max @ Ic=12mA, Ib=0.4mA (0.20V max @ Ic=24mA, Ib=1.0mA)
extra.Vbe(sat): 0.35V max @ Ic=12mA, Ib=0.4mA (0.40V max @ Ic=24mA, Ib=1.0mA)

typical_application: Low-frequency switching and general-purpose audio amplification. Historically the transistor in the Maestro Fuzz-Tone FZ-1; also widely used across early-1960s consumer electronics as a jellybean germanium switch/amplifier.
gotchas: TO-5 orientation matters: verify the case tab against pin 1 (emitter) before wiring, do not assume a silicon TO-92's E-B-C order carries over
germanium: leakage current (ICBO/IEBO) is far more temperature-sensitive than silicon; stay well below rated Pd and avoid letting it run hot
absolute ratings are low by modern standards (25V/100mA/150mW); this is a small-signal switch, not a power transistor
2N404A is a tighter-spec version of the same part; pinout and package are identical
